items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'Dogs make great pets because they are loyal and friendly.' What is the key idea?
A) Dogs are animals
B) Dogs are loyal and friendly, which makes them great pets
C) Dogs are bigger than cats
items.answer: B) Dogs are loyal and friendly, which makes them great pets

steps: The key idea captures the main point. The passage says dogs make great pets because of their loyalty and friendliness.

items.prompt:
After a read-aloud, a teacher asks: 'What happened first in the story?' What kind of question is this?
A) A question about a key detail
B) A question about the author's name
C) A question about your favorite part
items.answer: A) A question about a key detail

steps: 'What happened first?' is asking for a specific detail about the order of events in the text.

items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'The library has thousands of books. You can borrow them for free with a library card.' What is one key detail?
A) Libraries are quiet
B) You can borrow books for free with a library card
C) Libraries are in every city
items.answer: B) You can borrow books for free with a library card

steps: This detail was directly stated in the passage. Options A and C were not mentioned.

items.prompt:
What does it mean to RETELL a story after a read-aloud?
A) To read the story yourself
B) To say the key events or ideas back in your own words
C) To guess what the story might be about
items.answer: B) To say the key events or ideas back in your own words

steps: Retelling means describing the key events or ideas from the text in your own words after hearing or reading it.

items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'Sunflowers turn to face the sun as it moves across the sky. This is called heliotropism.' What is the key detail?
A) Sunflowers are yellow
B) Sunflowers turn to face the sun — this is called heliotropism
C) Flowers need water to grow
items.answer: B) Sunflowers turn to face the sun — this is called heliotropism

steps: This is the key detail that was directly stated and given a name in the passage.

items.prompt:
Should a retelling include every single word from the read-aloud?
A) Yes — say every word exactly as it was read
B) No — include the key ideas and important details, not every word
C) No — only say one word from the whole text
items.answer: B) No — include the key ideas and important details, not every word

steps: A retelling captures the key ideas and important details. It does not need to repeat every word.

items.prompt:
A teacher reads about frogs. A student says: 'The passage was about frogs.' Is this a complete retelling?
A) Yes — naming the topic is enough
B) No — a retelling should include key ideas and details, not just the topic
C) Yes — all retelling needs is one sentence
items.answer: B) No — a retelling should include key ideas and details, not just the topic

steps: Saying 'it was about frogs' only names the topic. A retelling explains the key ideas: what did the passage say ABOUT frogs?

items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'In autumn, leaves change color because the tree stops making chlorophyll.' What is the key idea?
A) Autumn is a pretty season
B) Leaves change color in autumn because the tree stops making chlorophyll
C) Trees lose their leaves in winter
items.answer: B) Leaves change color in autumn because the tree stops making chlorophyll

steps: This is the main fact stated in the passage. Options A and C were not stated.

items.prompt:
After a read-aloud about penguins, a teacher asks: 'Where do emperor penguins live?' This is a question about:
A) A specific detail from the text
B) The student's opinion
C) Something unrelated to the read-aloud
items.answer: A) A specific detail from the text

steps: The question asks for a specific fact that would have been stated in the read-aloud about penguins.

items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'Rosa Parks was a brave woman who refused to give up her seat on a bus. Her action helped start the Civil Rights Movement.' What is the key idea?
A) Rosa Parks liked to ride buses
B) Rosa Parks was brave and her action helped start the Civil Rights Movement
C) Buses were important in the 1900s
items.answer: B) Rosa Parks was brave and her action helped start the Civil Rights Movement

steps: The key idea captures the main point of the passage: Rosa Parks' bravery and its importance.

items.prompt:
What is a KEY IDEA in a text?
A) The most interesting sentence
B) The most important point the author wants you to understand
C) The last sentence in the passage
items.answer: B) The most important point the author wants you to understand

steps: A key idea is the central point that the whole passage supports. It is not necessarily the most interesting or the last sentence.

items.prompt:
A teacher reads a story. Afterward she asks: 'What was the problem the main character had to solve?' This is a question about:
A) A key detail in the story's plot
B) The student's favorite character
C) The title of the book
items.answer: A) A key detail in the story's plot

steps: The problem the character faces is a key plot detail. The teacher is asking the student to recall specific information from the read-aloud.

items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'The Amazon rainforest is home to more than half of the world's plant and animal species.' What key detail does this give?
A) The Amazon is a large river
B) The Amazon rainforest contains more than half of the world's species
C) Rainforests have a lot of rain
items.answer: B) The Amazon rainforest contains more than half of the world's species

steps: This is the specific fact stated in the passage. The other options were not stated.

items.prompt:
Which would be the BEST retelling of a passage about making bread?
A) 'Bread is delicious.'
B) 'To make bread, you mix flour, water, yeast, and salt, then let it rise, and bake it.'
C) 'I eat bread for lunch sometimes.'
items.answer: B) 'To make bread, you mix flour, water, yeast, and salt, then let it rise, and bake it.'

steps: Option B retells the key process — the steps and ingredients. Options A and C are personal reactions, not retellings from the text.

items.prompt:
After a read-aloud, a student says: 'I learned that the Great Wall of China is thousands of miles long and was built to protect China.' Is this a good retelling?
A) No — personal learning statements do not count
B) Yes — the student identified a key fact and its purpose from the text
C) No — a retelling must be longer than one sentence
items.answer: B) Yes — the student identified a key fact and its purpose from the text

steps: The student stated a specific fact (thousands of miles long) and its purpose (protect China) — these are key ideas from the read-aloud. This is a good, concise retelling.
